name: Nduga
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: De duidelijkheid van hun spreken laat weinig te wenschen over, en werd ook 't door ons teruggegeven woord nagenoeg altijd onmiddellijk herkend, waarbij het van groot voordeel was, dat de klemtoon steeds op de laatste lettergreep der woorden valt. ¹ [footnote 1:] Een uitzondering maakt het woord „hālĕbok" met den klemtoon op de eerste lettergreep tenzij „hā" als een afzonderlijk woord moet worden opgevat.
new_statements.translation: The clarity of their speech leaves little to be desired, and the word we repeated back was almost always recognised immediately, in which it was of great advantage that the stress always falls on the last syllable of the words. [footnote 1:] An exception is the word "hālĕbok" [a greeting], with the stress on the first syllable, unless "hā" is to be taken as a separate word.
new_statements.citation: van Nouhuys, J. W. 1912. Eerste bijdrage tot de kennis van de taal der "Pësëgem" van Centraal Nieuw-Guinea. Verzameld tijdens de expeditie 1909/1910 naar het Sneeuwgebergte. new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress always falls on the final syllable; the only exception noted is the greeting hālĕbok, stressed on the first syllable (which the author suspects is really hā + lĕbok).
new_statements.exceptions: One: the greeting word hālĕbok (elsewhere in the list 'ha-lë-bok'), stressed on the first syllable unless 'hā' is a separate word.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated words elicited by pointing and repetition during a first contact (29 Oct 1909 onward, Lorentz expedition), i.e. citation forms; the author is an explorer, not a linguist, and warns the list was compiled 'tijdens eene zeer vluchtige allereerste kennismaking' (during a very hasty first acquaintance). No phoneme inventory; the hyphenated transcriptions (e.g. në-nem-deh, sap-tjap) mark syllables, not stress.
new_statements.identity_note: The only stress statement is about the 'Pësëgem' (Pesegem/Pesechem) met by the 1909-10 Lorentz expedition in the valley between the Treub and Wichmann ranges (c. 4°28'S 138°43'E, 1500-1700 m, per van Nouhuys p. 266). Glottolog 5.1 lists Pesegem/Pesechem as alternate names of Nduga [ndug1245] and assigns van Nouhuys 1912 and Le Roux 1950 to it, but Voorhoeve 1975 (p. 37) files 'Pesechem' under a separate 'SOUTH NGALIK' entry (no. 65, sources Le Roux 1950, Bromley 1967), distinct from 'NDUGA (Ndugwa)' (no. 66); 'South Ngalik' is today an alternate name of Silimo [wul, sili1249] (Glottolog point -4.53, 139.00), while Nduga's point is -4.34, 138.41 and the Pesegem site lies between them. Treat the statement as Nduga per Glottolog's assignment, with the caveat that it may belong to a neighbouring Ngalik variety; the language is also called Kenyam Niknene (Peta Bahasa, via id-wiki) and has dialects Hitadipa Nduga and Sinak Nduga (find.bible).

sources.note: fetched sources now (Wayback copy of papuaerfgoed.org PDF, text layer present). Silent on stress, but p. 193 fixes the identity: the Noord river (Pesechem 'Wusak') separates the Pesechems from the Woeliks (= Wulik = Silimo), so Pesechem is not South Ngalik/Silimo, supporting Glottolog's Pesegem = Nduga assignment; also notes numerals 1-3 and that speakers 'swallow syllables'.

sources.citation: Snell, L. A. 1913. Eenige gegevens betreffende de kennis der zeden, gewoonten en taal der Pesechem van Centraal Nieuw-Guinea. Bulletin van de Maatschappij ter Bevordering van het Natuurkundig Onderzoek der Nederlandsche Koloniën 68.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Snell was the military lieutenant of the Third South New Guinea Expedition who lived for months in the Pesechem (Oro) valley in 1912-13 and compiled a much longer wordlist than van Nouhuys (Pulle 1915 p. 193); this is the earliest article whose title names the Pesechem language and the most likely place for a considered accent remark that would confirm or overturn the 1912 one-liner. Cited by nl.wikipedia 'Pesegem'. Not in Delpher, archive.org or the Leiden repository search from our machine; the Bulletin series may be on natuurtijdschriften.nl (Naturalis).
